name: Unspent Fury

detectability.signature: A churning violet-white cloud of magnetically confined plasma; broadband electromagnetic screaming punctuated by radiation spikes that saturate detectors

proximity: Sensor ghosts and false readings multiply as the storm's interference reaches out
Hull surfaces begin to ionize, glowing faintly at sharp edges
contact: Power systems overload and drain unpredictably within seconds
Plasma discharge arcs fuse to hulls and burn through unprotected plating
prolonged_exposure: Complete ship destruction as sustained arc discharge erodes structural members
Radiation exposure exceeding safe limits for any crew in shielded sections

phenomena: Visible plasma discharge arcs leaping hundreds of thousands of kilometers between filaments
Radiation spikes at irregular intervals that defy all modeling
Electromagnetic interference patterns that paint phantom ships on every scope
Hull ionization producing ghostly corona effects on nearby vessels
hazards: Power system overload cascading into life support failure
Radiation exposure exceeding safe limits within minutes of contact
Complete ship destruction from sustained plasma arcing
opportunities: Energy harvesting potential for properly hardened collection rigs
Data valuable to scientific institutions studying self-sustaining plasma confinement
known_incidents: The harvesting rig Copper Kettle operated inside the storm's rim for eleven profitable days before an unforecast surge vaporized her and her crew of forty
Three neighboring colonies lost grid power simultaneously when a discharge arc jumped the intervening space in 2388
description: Unspent Fury is a storm eight-tenths of an astronomical unit wide and growing, a slow cyclone of violet-white plasma with no star to explain it. Its filaments crawl around one another in braids visible from system's edge, and its electromagnetic voice saturates every band with something between a scream and a hymn. No cataclysm birthed it; it simply has been burning, alone, for sixty-two million years.

The storm expands at roughly a kilometer per second, swallowing dust, ice, and anything slower. Discharge arcs leap between filaments without warning, and its radiation spikes follow no distribution any statistician will defend. Ships caught on its rim report instruments showing them friendly contacts that were never there, followed by hull edges beginning to glow.

The Copper Kettle proved the storm could be farmed: eleven days of record energy harvest before an unforecast surge took her and forty hands in under a second. Her sister rigs still work the receding edge at greater caution and greater distance. The 2388 arc-jump that blacked out three colonies added a new line to every insurance policy in the sector.

Harvest consortia maintain picket stations beyond the four-million-kilometer warning line, betting against the next surge. Physicists would trade much to know what has fed the storm since before Earth developed forests. Captains crossing the region carry triple sensor redundancy and a superstition apiece, and neither redundancy nor superstition has yet failed anyone who also kept their distance.
